data-model.title: Data model & provenance
body: Every Gold dataset published under data/public/gold/ is a Parquet file with provenance metadata embedded in the Arrow schema, under the "climasus_meta" key (written by climasus4r::write_parquet_climasus()). This metadata includes the source DATASUS system, pipeline stage, aggregation type, and a processing history.

Versioning follows vX.Y.Z per dataset (e.g. health_climate_daily/v1.0.0). The path is always gold/{dataset}/v{version}/uf={uf}/data.parquet — the schema is identical between synthetic and real versions, so nothing in the frontend needs to change when a dataset moves from prototype to real data.
data/public/catalog.json lists every published dataset; each has a sibling datapackage.json (Frictionless Data standard) with the full schema and the same provenance metadata.

querying.title: Querying with DuckDB-WASM
body: climasusDB has no backend: the browser runs a WebAssembly build of DuckDB and queries the published Parquet files directly via HTTP range requests — only the bytes needed for each query are downloaded.

The same Parquet files can be opened outside the platform, with no dependency on climasusDB at all: with the DuckDB CLI (SELECT * FROM read_parquet('URL')), with pandas/pyarrow in Python, or with arrow::read_parquet() in R.
Example query used by Explore: SELECT code_muni, avg(tmax) FROM health_climate_daily GROUP BY code_muni.

catalog-contract.title: Catalog contract
body: catalog.json guarantees: dataset name, latest version, list of available versions, synthetic-data flag, relative Parquet path, and row count. datapackage.json guarantees the column schema and the full climasus_meta metadata.

Tabular datasets (like health_climate_daily) use this Frictionless Data contract, not STAC. The STAC catalog (build_stac.R) is reserved for future gridded raster datasets (ERA5, CHIRPS) once those are published — this avoids duplicating two cataloging systems for the same tabular data type.

heat-cardio.title: Heat and mortality in Rondônia
body: This theme applies to Rondônia's published data the same methodological approach from a climasus4r case study on cardiovascular mortality in the elderly and heatwaves: detect heatwave events (WHO/WMO methods) from INMET station temperature series and relate them to the daily death series per municipality.

The published datasets backing this theme are health_climate_daily (daily deaths and climate per municipality, 2018–2023) and heatwave_events (heatwave events detected at RO's INMET stations, with a severity index and intensity class).
For the full statistical methodology (DLNM, attributable burden), see the corresponding advanced-modeling tutorial in the climasus4r documentation.
